$comment: `retrieval_text` is the SUBJECT of a request, distilled for the engine's rare-token gate and, when it differs from `query`, the semantic query. Two production entrances build it — home chat (next/lib/mcp/scopeQueryRouter.ts::buildRetrievalQueryText) and scheduled routines (control_plane/scope_query_router.py::build_retrieval_query_text) — and until 2026-09-06 only the first removed output-shape words and style spans, so a scheduled report asked the node about its own instructions. This file is the contract both entrances are tested against: the vocabularies, the algorithm, and reference vectors. The app is the reference implementation and `next/scripts/emit-retrieval-text-contract.ts` regenerates every copy from it (engine, control plane, app); `--check` fails when any copy differs. Vector inputs are invented sentences (the transform catalogue, pinned routine prompts, edge cases) — never text from a real node; this file ships in the public wheel.

engine: semantic query: needle_text replaces query_text for the vector lane when it differs

algorithm: 1. dates = extract_date_expressions(raw) — verbatim, first-occurrence order, deduped case-insensitively
2. body = raw with every date span replaced by a single space
3. body = body with every style span replaced by a single space (style_span.patterns; case-insensitive, all occurrences)
4. tokens = body trimmed, capped at query_text_max characters, lowercased, matched by intent_token_pattern; keywords = tokens minus stop_words, deduped keeping order, first intent_keyword_cap
5. fewer than two keywords means nothing distillable: the result is raw, untouched (never a placeholder, never the stripped body)
6. subject = keywords minus output_shape_words, joined by single spaces
7. text = subject followed by the dates, joined by single spaces, trimmed; empty text falls back to raw; the result is capped at query_text_max characters

parts: segment_request_parts(raw) minus the preamble; fewer than two sections means no parts; each section goes through steps 1-7; fewer than two non-empty needles means no parts. A one-keyword section therefore falls back to its own raw text, enumerator included ('1) how did I sleep') — identical at both entrances, by design.
